tagline.text: A limestone cave about 3 km long and a white-sand beach on Hikdop Island, just off Surigao City

location.label: Location
location.text: Pagkawasan, Barangay Buenavista, Hikdop Island, Surigao City, Surigao del Norte

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–1,500 (typical boat hire rate, confirm locally)

children.text: A limestone cave on Hikdop Island, a short boat ride from Surigao City. It has three entrances and a total length of about 3 km, and inside you will find a rock cluster known as the King's Throne and a knee-deep pool. After the cave, the island's white-sand beach is a pleasant place to rest.

Buenavista Cave is a limestone cave on Hikdop Island, in the sea right off the mainland of Surigao City. Administratively it belongs to Barangay Buenavista, Surigao City, Surigao del Norte, and the village from which you climb to the cave is listed under the name Pagkawasan. Hikdop Island lies closer to Dinagat Island than to the Mindanao mainland, so from the Surigao City waterfront it looks like a small island floating on the sea.

The cave is a karst cave formed by dissolving limestone, and its main sights are the stalactites that grew where water dripped from the ceiling and the stalagmites that rose from the floor. The cave database Showcaves lists the length as about 3,000 m with three entrances, and notes that there is no lighting inside. Showcaves and travel guides alike describe a rock cluster deep inside, called King's Court or King's Throne. The cluster is said to look like a huge crowd of people standing together. Guides differ slightly on whether the two names refer to the same section, so it is best to ask your local guide directly.

About 100 m from the large entrance there is an underground pool that is roughly knee-deep. The main entrance is known for a squeeze through a gap where boulders have collapsed, which opens into a large chamber. Bats live in the cave, and one guide mentions unusual species of bats and snakes. The area near the entrance is good for photos, but further in there are climbs and fallen rocks, so you need reasonable fitness and proper footwear.

This cave is quiet because it is not as famous as Siargao or Sohoton Cove. It suits travelers passing through Surigao City who want an easy island trip, and first-time cavers. However, there are almost no facilities or signs, and official information on fees and opening hours is hard to find, so it is important to check locally before you set out. In short, the trip goes like this: hire a motorboat on the Surigao City waterfront and cross to Hikdop Island, register in Pagkawasan village, then enter the cave. After the cave, relax on the beach and return by boat, and the whole outing takes half a day. If you have time left, you can add a museum or another cave in Surigao City on the same day.
The cave is known to have three entrances and is described as about
3 km

long. The main entrance is on the Pagkawasan village side, and once you pass through the gap between collapsed boulders, a large chamber opens up. The stretch that visitors actually walk is much shorter, so decide the route together with your guide. Because there are three entrances, your experience can differ depending on which one you enter and which you exit by.

Deep inside there is a rock structure that looks like a royal throne, which is why it is called the King's Throne. Showcaves calls a similar cluster King's Court and says it resembles a huge crowd of people standing together. It is the signature scene of cave photos here.
About
inside the large entrance there is a knee-deep pool. Expect to get wet and choose your footwear accordingly. The cool water refreshes you if you are tired from the heat.

Old, blackened stalactites hang from the ceiling, and stalagmites and stones of many shapes cover the floor. Touching damages the surface, so look with your eyes only, and never write on or damage the formations.
Bats live in the cave. Courtesy means not shining your lantern on the ceiling for long or making loud noises that startle them. Areas with many bats can smell, so a mask is handy.

Hikdop Island has Pagkawasan Beach, a stretch of fine white sand lined with coconut trees. There are cottages where you can rest, and it is a good place to wash off sweat and dirt in the sea after caving. Guides note that the area has no electricity but a good mobile signal. Some visitors also say the water is an emerald color on clear days and good for swimming.

blocks.title: A short boat ride from Surigao

children.text: Sources differ on the boat ride from the Surigao City waterfront, giving anywhere from
20 minutes
to
45 minutes
. It varies with wind and the type of boat, so confirm the exact time and your return time with the boatman before leaving.
Find a boat at the Surigao City waterfront boat landing and agree on the fare and your return time in advance. Fares are usually settled by bargaining.
Set off for Hikdop Island. Depending on the source, the boat ride is
20 minutes
to
45 minutes
, so allow some slack.
Arrive at Pagkawasan village and check with the village office or a local guide about visitor registration and whether a guide must accompany you. Pay any fee at this point.
Enter the cave and see the large entrance, the big inner chamber, the King's Throne section and the knee-deep pool in turn. Allow about
1 hour 30 minutes
for a comfortable visit.
Come out to the beach, wash off the sweat and dirt in the sea, and have lunch. It is safer to bring packed food and drinking water from the mainland.
Return by boat to the Surigao City waterfront.
If you spend longer in the cave, shorten your beach time. If sea conditions worsen, boats may not be able to go out, so it is better to make the trip in the morning.

items.title: From Surigao City to Hikdop Island

children.text: Hire a motorboat at the Surigao City waterfront and boat landing. A local blog says you can rent a motorboat at the landing near the city boulevard.
The boat ride takes about
20 minutes
to
45 minutes
depending on the source.
The general price range for island tours is given as about ₱1,000–1,500, but no confirmed boat fare for this cave exists, so you will need to negotiate locally.

items.title: From other areas by land and sea

children.text: You can reach Surigao City by bus from the direction of Butuan or Davao. From Butuan it is described as taking about
3 hours
Ferries run to and from the Surigao City port from Cebu, Maasin and Siargao.

In the rain the cave floor becomes slippery and the pool can rise, so the drier months are safer. The Surigao area has a long and frequent rainy season, so given the boat ride, the most important thing is to pick a day when the sea is calm.
Exact monthly rainfall and sea conditions differ from year to year, so check the weather forecast and port advisories a few days before you go.

The time of day matters for the boat as well. On some days the wind picks up in the afternoon, so crossing in the morning and returning early is generally safer. Inside the cave it is cool even when it is hot outside, but humidity is high and sweat does not dry easily, so a change of clothes is handy.

Hikdop Island is described as having almost no lodging and no electricity, so most people stay in Surigao City and visit on a day trip. Surigao City is said to have inexpensive pensions and apartelles around Capitol Road and San Nicolas Street, but the price information is old, so confirm before booking.

Assume the island has almost no restaurants, and bring lunch and drinking water from the mainland. You may be able to eat while resting in the cottages at Pagkawasan Beach, but whether anything is sold can vary from day to day.

Surigao City is a gateway with boats to Siargao, Leyte and Cebu, so there is a range of lodging for travelers. The airport and bus terminal are each about 4 km from downtown, so if you want to catch an early-morning boat, it is easier to stay near the waterfront downtown. In the evening you can get a simple meal on the streets near the pier. Sleep well the night before caving, and eat lightly on the morning of your trip.
Before leaving, clearly agree on the boat fare, the return time and the waiting time with the boatman.
Cave first, swim afterward. You can wash off sweat and dirt in the sea straight away.
There is no lighting in the cave, so bring a headlamp and a backup light.
Non-slip shoes that can get wet, long trousers and gloves are handy.
Take a local guide. Someone who knows the way keeps you safe and can explain what you see.
Bring drinking water, snacks, a trash bag and cash in small bills from the mainland.
Bring a waterproof pouch for your phone and a change of clothes.
Combining it with other sights in Surigao City works well. Visiting places such as Silop Multi-Caves or Sagisi Island on separate days is also a good plan.
Inside the cave, set a front-and-back order so your group does not scatter, and carry spare batteries in case a lantern dies.
Sunscreen can wash off in the sea, so apply it once more before you reach the beach. Take all your trash back with you.

The cave is dark and the floor can be slippery, and an older visitor account (2008) mentions fallen rocks and little supervision. Check current conditions locally, and do not go in alone; go with a guide.
The cave has no lighting, and some sections have steep climbs and narrow gaps. Consider your fitness and condition and do not push yourself.
Visitor accounts say the cave has been damaged by graffiti and carvings on the walls. Leave no marks of any kind.
Some passages are reportedly hard to pass because of collapsed rocks. If the way is blocked, turn back.
If it rains or the sea is rough, both the cave and the boat are dangerous, so postpone your plan.
There are no lifeguards on the beach. Take special care with children and anyone who cannot swim.
Fees, registration rules and opening hours can change, so check the latest announcements and local advice.
A surfing island reachable by ferry from the Surigao City pier. Plan at least a day for it, separate from the cave.
